dedupe_keys.name: pvxte web tool for electric bus feasibility and fleet scheduling

description: PVxTE is an open-source web application that helps public transport operators judge whether they can move bus fleets from diesel to electric. It combines a non-linear mixed-integer optimisation for vehicle scheduling, battery charge and discharge limits and a graph method for the minimum number of drivers, then compares electric and diesel options on cost and emissions. Users supply bus specifications, terminals with elevation and charger data, a distance matrix, timetables and economic parameters, and it returns optimal fleet size and battery configuration, driver needs, investment and operating costs and energy use per kilometre. SUPSI built it in Python with Flask and funding from the Swiss Federal Office of Transport under the SETP 2050 programme; it is MIT licensed and free, with commits up to 25 November 2025. Caveats: results depend on operator-supplied inputs and the tool was not run. It suits capacity planning and optimisation of electric bus depots. Related catalogue record: model-routezero-electric-bus-depot-charging.
